activity.notes: Snorri Sturluson was an Icelandic chieftain, historian, poet and politician of the Icelandic Commonwealth. Snorrastofa records that he lived at Reykholt from 1206 until his death in 1241 and credits him with major works including the Edda and Heimskringla. ATLAS therefore uses a broad representative literary and scholarly Activity from c.1206 to 1241 rather than reducing him to either of his two non-contiguous terms as lawspeaker (1215–1218 and 1222–1231).

sources.title: Snorri Sturluson — Snorrastofa
sources.citation_text: Snorrastofa identifies Snorri as a chieftain, storyteller, politician, author and poet, credits him with Edda and Heimskringla, and describes his public career in thirteenth-century Iceland.

sources.title: Welcome to Snorrastofa in Reykholt, West Iceland
sources.citation_text: Snorrastofa states that Snorri lived in Reykholt from 1206 until his death in 1241 and highlights Heimskringla, Edda and Egil's Saga as works central to Northern European history.

sources.title: 90. mál, Hæstiréttur Íslands — Alþingi
sources.citation_text: The Icelandic parliament record notes Snorri's two lawspeaker terms, 1215–1218 and 1222–1231, supporting the decision not to flatten those interrupted offices into one formal term Activity.
